exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
cohort: 3,666 children participating in the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children (LSAC)
finding: Cesarean-born children had significantly lower cognitive performance scores compared to vaginally-born children, even after adjusting for confounders.
mod_finding: Cesarean-born children performed significantly below vaginally-born children across several cognitive performance measures.
